correctness.rationale: For full column rank A, the normal equations give r orthogonal to im(A), so H and Q are projectors of ranks n and n+1. Their k-minor sums are the respective binomial coefficients, by taking the coefficient of t^k in det(I+tH) and det(I+tQ). For each positive-probability S, H_SS is positive definite, the constraints are feasible, and minimizing the G-norm of x−x_* subject to A_S(x−x_*)=r_S adds exactly r_S^T H_SS^{-1} r_S to the squared residual. By the determinant lemma the per-set normalized loss is det Q_SS / det H_SS. In the average the denominator cancels only on the positive-probability support; adding and subtracting the remaining minors gives the exact formula and the upper equality criterion. The lower bound is pointwise. The Vandermonde and padded-identity constructions meet the two endpoints with nonzero residual for every allowed n,k. Independently checking the strict example gives x_*=(-3,15,1)/7, r=(10,3,13,13,-13)/7 and ||r||²=88/7. The only singular pair has H entries all 3/7 and u_1−u_2=1/||r||, so its augmented determinant is 3/88, giving ratio 175/88 and excess 87/7. This concerns loss inflation with access to every response, not mean parameter bias or a label-efficient regression procedure. CHECK.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed; the argument above is an independent exact check.

evidence: Dereziński–Warmuth Theorem 8 treats exactly d samples in dimension d; its proof handles zero-probability sets as the source of a potential strict bound.
Fanuel et al. Theorem 5.8 is a risk bound for a projected Nyström estimator under a variable-size law; Theorem 4.1 is a semiparametric DPP expectation identity.
Sun et al. analyze iterative convergence on consistent systems and list the inconsistent setting as a direction for future work.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The prior full-dimension loss principle overlaps the boundary k=n, which is explicitly excluded here. General determinant and DPP tools are applicable, but the inspected risk statements do not supply the exact deficit or the frontier at k<n.

evidence: The full-dimension interpolation factor is d+1, whereas the present factor is (n+1)/(n-k+1), reflecting optimization with n-k unconstrained directions.
For two finite laws on the same k-sets, averaging their likelihood ratio against H is the elementary mass-on-support identity used here.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The mass identity is mechanically known and gets no novelty credit. The known regression bounds do not allow changing k below parameter dimension while leaving the same n-dimensional objective. The distinct subdimension application requires the G-metric constrained-optimum formula and its connection to exactly the two nested projectors, plus examples showing the upper and lower factors are sharp.

evidence: The ratio is binom(n+1,k)/binom(n,k) times the likelihood ratio of the Q and H fixed-size DPP laws on the support of H.
Epperly defines the appropriate fixed-size minor laws, but the active regression result there interpolates k samples in a k-parameter model.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The DPP formulation identifies the deficit as probability mass for Q outside the support of H. Generic DPP theory gives that interpretation once the optimizer-to-minor identity is proved; it does not identify the loss of this full-design optimizer. The active-regression objective in the inspected result is not a relabeling of the subdimension hard-constraint problem.

value.rationale: This is an exact benchmark for the cost of retaining selected hard equations in an inconsistent least-squares system, when the full objective remains available. It answers for every design which upper-bound loss is lost to rank degeneracy, instead of silently treating zero-probability sets as zero augmented minors. The all-design endpoints and strict interior example make this distinction quantitative. This does not offer a convergence or label-efficiency guarantee.
